subject: Novamed — DPA redline: controller/processor roles + SCCs clarification
messages:
From: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@novamed.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.example
Cc: legal@novamed.com
Date: 2028-04-26T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA redline (v3) — controller/processor split and SCCs

Olga — thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching our consolidated DPA redline (Novamed_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Key items we flagged for your legal team: 

- Controller vs. processor language: we believe NovaMed should remain controller for patient-identifiable data; you previously proposed a narrower controller carveout in the Order Form. We need explicit confirmation in the DPA about which data classes are in scope for controller-led processing.
- SCCs: we expect the latest EU SCCs to be incorporated and for any subprocessor chains to be disclosed at signature.
- Transfer impact addendum: we asked for a short addendum describing hosting geolocation and fallback routing in case of on-prem failures.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the controller carveout for the analytics bucket only (pseudonymized telemetry), and remain processor for EHR ingestion? If not, please propose exact language. Also, do you have a timeline for final MSA + Order Form signoff?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we are targeting a pilot start in mid-May.

Thanks,
Amelia Hart
Head of Legal Operations
NovaMed

Attachments: Novamed_DPA_redline_v3.docx (docx, 124 KB)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.example
To: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@novamed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: 2028-04-26T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline (v3) — controller/processor split and SCCs

Amelia — received, thanks. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Ben (sales/procurement) to confirm internal posture. Quick take below; Karthik will follow with precise redline suggestions: 

- Controller/processor: Redwood's standard approach is to be processor for customer data ingestion (EHR) and controller only for aggregated telemetry used to improve the service. We're open to an Order Form carveout that explicitly lists data categories treated as controller-owned. We prefer that carving be narrow and scoped to pseudonymized analytics.
- SCCs: we accept incorporation of the latest EU SCCs subject to our standard MSA cross-references. We will need to confirm subprocessor disclosure cadence (we usually provide quarterly notices).
- Transfer addendum: we can provide a short transfer-impact addendum describing regions, KMS jurisdictions, and fallback routing. Clarify whether you need the addendum to be contractual or informational.

Action items: 
1) Karthik: produce redline language for a narrow analytics carveout + SCC insertion (by EOD).
2) Ben: confirm procurement timeline and whether we can close MSA + Order Form by 2028-05-10 to keep pilot date.
3) Amelia: does your team require a signed subprocessor list prior to signature, or is a covenant to produce it within 7 days acceptable?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: OrderForm_2028-04-20.pdf (pdf, 68 KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: olga.petrov@redwood.example, Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@novamed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: 2028-04-26T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline (v3) — proposed language

Amelia / Olga / Ben — drafting note and proposed text below. I'm attaching inline excerpts in the body so you can paste them into your doc quickly.

1) Controller carveout (analytics bucket): 
Proposed insertion (DPA §2.1, new clause): "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this DPA, Customer shall be the Controller with respect to Pseudonymized Telemetry Data as defined in Schedule A ("Analytics Data"). Redwood shall be a Processor for all other Customer Data. The Parties agree that Analytics Data shall be limited to aggregated, pseudonymized metrics that cannot be reasonably re-identified to a natural person without additional Customer-held data."

2) SCCs: 
We will incorporate the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (2021 version) as an Annex and reference processor obligations. Redwood requests the right to update the SCC Annex to reflect future Commission updates with notice and a right to object on reasonable grounds.

3) Subprocessor disclosure cadence: 
We can commit to publishing the subprocessor list at signature and updating quarterly; if Novamed requires earlier disclosure for a named critical subprocessor, please list them.

4) Transfer impact addendum: 
Proposal: a short addendum that states primary hosting regions (eu-west-1), KMS key jurisdiction (DE), and fallback routing policy. We propose the addendum be informational and non-amendatory to the core DPA, but we can allow it to be contractual on a case-by-case basis with specific Order Form tie-out.

If Novamed accepts the above, I'll produce an edited DPA v3 marked in Word and return by 17:00 UTC. Otherwise, flag specific language to negotiate.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.example
To: olga.petrov@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-04-26T16:35:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline (v3) — timeline confirmation

Team / Amelia — quick procurement note: Novamed's procurement indicated legal signoff is the last blocker; commercial terms are locked. We can meet the 2028-05-10 go/no-go if Redwood returns a cleaned DPA and Order Form by EOD 2028-04-29. Key commercial asks from Novamed: 

- No post-signature surcharge for SCC updates; they want SCC updates included in the MSA change control if required by law.
- A 30-day onboarding SLA commitment in the Order Form (we can offer reasonable language).

Amelia — can your team confirm acceptance of the proposed subprocessor cadence (publish at signature + quarterly updates)? If yes, Karthik and Olga will mark and we'll aim to send final docs Friday. If Novamed needs the transfer addendum to be contractual, confirm and we'll have legal weigh in on potential pricing impact.

Thanks all — I’ll coordinate signatures once legal confirms.

Ben Carter
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
